correctness.rationale: The transformed density is explicitly continuous at the cotangent endpoint. Absolute Poisson Fourier convergence proves the all-node alias identity. The odd derivative is strictly negative except individual matched scales; mixture nondegeneracy guarantees global strictness. For even node counts the factored second logarithmic derivative has a positive bracket and at worst isolated zeros, yielding strict convexity and unique global minimizers. Extreme-scale dominance and signed balance prove the common log-scale asymptotic; equal-weight two-scale reflection and root comparison prove the exact and strict monotonic refinements. The extracted verifier passed 1898 finite checks, supplementing but not proving the all-n claims.

value.rationale: The literature specifically motivates Möbius quadrature of heavy-tailed Cauchy weights; a positive mixture is the first natural nontrivial density where no single matched scale flattens all components. The theorem supplies a complete global parameter rule and exact odd/even feasibility boundary, including a finite-node closed optimum and sharp exponential asymptotic cost of even sampling. This is a motivated, structurally informative calibration benchmark rather than a bare normalization check, and it does not need a downstream general theorem to be valuable.
